abstract.t: In this document, we introduce a new BGP capability that allows the advertisement of a BGP speaker's routing software version.

This BGP capability is an optional advertisement. Implementations are not required to advertise the version nor to process received advertisements. The capability is intended only for use within networks under common administrative control, primarily for troubleshooting and debugging purposes in environments such as containerized BGP deployments where alternative version discovery mechanisms are inadequate.

This document includes comprehensive analysis of security risks, including fingerprinting and targeted exploitation concerns, and provides strict guidance on appropriate and inappropriate deployment scenarios.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: In modern data center designs, conventional routers participate in routing. These routers may have different versions of routing software. Knowing which versions of the routing software are running on the various routers in the network can be a crucial factor in quickly identifying the root cause of protocol or network problems.

This document specifies a BGP capability that carries the routing software version. This BGP capability is optional. Implementations are not required to advertise their software version nor to process it on receipt. Due to significant security implications described in , the capability MUST be disabled by default and MUST only be enabled in carefully controlled environments where the operational benefits justify the security risks.

Information about the version of the routing software could also be exchanged in protocols such as LLDP and CDP. However, in containerized environments, it is difficult and not recommended to exchange this information between background processes. To assist in minimizing operational costs in such environments, it is helpful to exchange the routing software versions between BGP peers directly. The rationale for using BGP rather than alternative mechanisms is discussed in detail below.

section.name: Rationale for BGP-based Version Advertisement
section.t: This section addresses why BGP is an appropriate mechanism for version advertisement in specific operational environments, particularly containerized BGP deployments.

section.name: Operational Context
section.t: Modern network operations increasingly deploy BGP speakers in containerized environments where traditional inventory and monitoring approaches face significant challenges. In these environments:

ul.li: BGP speakers run in isolated containers with minimal tooling and no direct access to host-level inventory systems
Container orchestration systems may dynamically create, destroy, and migrate BGP speakers across physical hosts
Traditional LLDP and CDP operate at Layer 2 and cannot traverse the virtual networking layers common in containerized deployments
Multiple BGP speaker containers may run on the same physical host, making physical-layer identification ambiguous

section.name: Why Existing Approaches Are Insufficient
section.t: While inventory management systems can identify what software versions are supposed to be running, they face critical operational gaps:

ul.li: Container image tags may not reflect actual running code (e.g., due to local modifications, rollbacks, or deployment errors)
External inventory systems require additional authentication, authorization, and network paths to query
Debugging connectivity issues may require knowing the peer's version before external inventory systems are accessible
Real-time troubleshooting during BGP session establishment failures benefits from immediate version visibility without querying external systems

section.t: The BGP protocol session itself provides an authenticated, direct communication channel between peers that is available precisely when version information is most valuable for debugging.

section.name: Specific Use Cases
section.t: The primary intended use cases are:

ul.li: Rapid identification of version-specific bugs during BGP session establishment or operation
Automated correlation of BGP behavior anomalies with known software issues across a fleet of routers
Verification that intended software versions are actually running after upgrades or rollbacks
Operational visibility in environments where BGP speakers are the only directly accessible component (e.g., route reflectors in Kubernetes clusters)

Network troubleshooting using packet captures: when analyzing BGP OPEN messages in packet captures (e.g., using tcpdump, Wireshark, or similar tools), the version capability allows immediate identification of the software version used by each peer without requiring access to the devices themselves or external inventory systems. This is particularly valuable when troubleshooting historical issues from archived packet captures or when analyzing traffic from devices that are no longer accessible.

section.t: These use cases are specifically scoped to environments under common administrative control where the debugging benefits justify accepting the security risks described in .

section.name: Specification of Requirements
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Software Version Capability
section.t: Although this document is not an IETF Standards Track document, it makes use of the terminology from BCP 14 in order to clearly state the implementation behaviors.

BGP capability advertisement is defined in . BGP Capabilities contain one or more triples <Capability Code, Capability Length, Capability Value>. This document defines a new BGP capability, the Software Version Capability, with Capability Code 75 and Capability Length and Capability Value as described below.

The inclusion of the Software Version Capability is OPTIONAL. If an implementation supports the inclusion of the capability, the implementation MUST include a configuration option to enable or disable its use, and MUST default to disabled.

The Software Version Capability is intended ONLY for environments where more visibility is needed for troubleshooting purposes within a trust boundary. It is NOT RECOMMENDED for use outside a single Autonomous System, or a set of Autonomous Systems under a common administration. It MUST NOT be enabled on BGP sessions that cross organizational or administrative boundaries without explicit agreement from both parties and thorough evaluation of the security risks described in .

Implementations SHOULD provide configuration mechanisms that make it difficult to accidentally enable this capability on external BGP sessions, such as requiring per-session or per-peer-group explicit configuration rather than global enablement.
An implementation that does not recognize or support the Software Version Capability but receives one must ignore it, as described in .
The triple for the Software Version Capability is as follows:
Capability Code
Capability Length

ul.li: Capability Length is a one-octet unsigned binary integer that contains the length of the Capability Value field in octets.
The Capability Length for the Software Version Capability MUST be greater than zero. A value of zero SHALL be treated as an encoding error and the Capability MUST be ignored.
The Capability Length SHOULD be no greater than 64. This length leaves space for other capabilities.

section.t: Capability Value

ul.li: The Capability Value field is the software version encoded as a UTF-8 string. It is unstructured data and can be formatted in any way that the implementor decides. The string is not null-terminated.

section.t: Version:

ul.li: The Version field MUST be encoded using UTF-8. A receiving BGP speaker MUST NOT interpret invalid UTF-8 sequences.
The value consists of one identifier, which identifies the software and its significant version. Software version identifier consists of a product and optional product version.
identifier = product ["/" product-version]

A sender SHOULD limit generated product identifiers to what is necessary to identify the product; a sender MUST NOT generate advertising or other nonessential information within the product identifier. A sender SHOULD NOT generate information in product-version that is not a version identifier (i.e., successive versions of the same product name ought to differ only in the product-version portion of the product identifier).
Example:
frrouting/8.4.2, ios/12.5.1, junos/12.1

section.name: Capabilities Length Overflow
section.t: As defined in [RFC5492] the total length of capabilities that can be carried by the BGP Capabilities Optional Parameter is 255 bytes. If an implementation is constructing a BGP Capabilities Optional Parameter and its length exceeds 255 bytes, there is not enough space for other more important capabilities.
Implementations of this specification are REQUIRED Extended Optional Parameters Length for BGP OPEN Message support as defined in .

section.name: Operation
section.t: The Software Version Capability MUST only be used for displaying the version of a BGP speaker's router daemon to make troubleshooting easier.

Consider a group of routers each with a number of upstream nodes, and suppose that each router has a different operating system and different routing software at a different installed version. Assuming that a specific feature is not working or that there is a bug which has not been fixed in a particular version of the code, knowledge of the routing daemon versions would allow an operator to quickly identify the pattern of which versions are affected.

A particularly valuable operational scenario involves packet capture analysis. When troubleshooting BGP session establishment problems or analyzing protocol behavior, operators often capture network traffic using tools such as tcpdump or Wireshark. The Software Version Capability appears in the BGP OPEN message and is therefore immediately visible in the packet capture. This allows operators to identify the exact software version of both peers without needing:

ul.li: Interactive access to the BGP speaker devices
Access to external inventory or management systems
Correlation with separate logging or monitoring data

section.t: This is especially useful when analyzing packet captures from production incidents after the fact, when reviewing archived captures, or when troubleshooting issues reported by remote teams who can provide packet captures but may not have detailed system access.

Enabling (i.e., turning on) this capability requires bouncing all existing BGP sessions and the feature MUST be explicitly configured before an implementation advertizes the Software Version Capability.

section.name: Deployment Status and Recommendations
section.t: This section documents the current deployment status of the Software Version Capability and provides guidance on appropriate deployment scenarios.

section.name: Current Implementation Status
section.t: At the time of writing, the Software Version Capability has been implemented in several known BGP implementations and tools:

ul.li: FRRouting
GoBGP
freeRouter
ExaBGP
Flock networks
Wireshark

section.t: Deployment of the capability in production networks is believed to be limited primarily to internal/iBGP sessions within single organizations, particularly in containerized and cloud-native environments where traditional inventory mechanisms are insufficient.

The capability has proven valuable for its intended debugging and troubleshooting use cases in these controlled environments. However, widespread deployment across organizational boundaries has not occurred and is explicitly NOT RECOMMENDED by this document.

section.name: Recommended Deployment Scenarios
section.t: This capability is designed for and RECOMMENDED only in the following scenarios:

ul.li: iBGP sessions within a single Autonomous System
BGP sessions between ASes under unified administrative control (e.g., multiple ASes of the same organization)
Route reflector infrastructures within data centers
Containerized BGP environments where alternative version discovery is impractical
Laboratory, testing, and development environments

section.t: In all cases, deployment MUST be limited to environments where all BGP speakers are trusted and under administrative control of the deploying organization.

section.name: Explicitly Discouraged Deployment Scenarios
section.t: This capability MUST NOT be deployed in the following scenarios:

ul.li: eBGP sessions with Internet service providers
eBGP sessions with customers
eBGP sessions with peers at Internet exchange points
Any BGP session crossing organizational trust boundaries
BGP sessions with external parties who have not explicitly agreed to exchange this information
Default configurations or deployment templates that apply to unspecified sessions

section.t: The use of this capability on any BGP session with an untrusted or external party exposes the deploying organization to the security risks described in without corresponding benefits.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA has assigned capability number 75 for the Software Version Capability described in this document. This registration is in the BGP Capability Codes registry.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This section provides a comprehensive analysis of the security risks associated with advertising software version information over BGP, and guidance on when and how to deploy this capability safely.

section.name: Threat Model and Attack Vectors
section.t: The Software Version Capability exposes implementation details that create several categories of security risk:

section.name: Fingerprinting Attacks
section.t: Version information enables attackers to precisely identify the BGP implementation and version, facilitating targeted exploitation of known vulnerabilities. An attacker who can observe BGP OPEN messages (either through network access or compromised infrastructure) gains:

ul.li: Exact software version information for exploit targeting
Knowledge of which CVEs and security advisories apply
Ability to enumerate network infrastructure and identify high-value targets
Intelligence for planning multi-stage attacks

section.t: This risk is significantly elevated when the capability is used on inter-provider links or any BGP sessions involving untrusted parties.

section.name: Feature Proxy and Implementation Inference
section.t: Beyond direct exploitation, version information can serve as a proxy for inferring:

ul.li: Which BGP features and extensions are likely supported
Performance characteristics and scaling limitations
Vendor and operational practices
Network architecture and design patterns

section.t: This information asymmetry may advantage competitors or adversaries in both technical and business contexts.

section.name: Risk vs. Benefit Analysis
section.t: Deployment of this capability MUST be preceded by careful analysis of whether the operational benefits outweigh the security risks in the specific deployment context.

section.name: When Benefits May Outweigh Risks
section.t: The capability is most appropriate in environments where:

ul.li: All BGP speakers are under common administrative control (single Autonomous System or tightly coordinated ASes)
Network access is strictly controlled and monitored
BGP sessions use authentication and encryption (e.g., TCP-AO, IPsec)
Rapid troubleshooting of version-specific issues provides substantial operational value
Alternative version discovery mechanisms are unavailable or inadequate (e.g., containerized environments)
The organization has mature security practices including timely patching and vulnerability management

section.name: When Risks Clearly Outweigh Benefits
section.t: The capability SHOULD NOT be deployed when:

ul.li: BGP sessions cross organizational boundaries (inter-provider BGP)
Sessions are with customers, peers, or other external parties
Network security posture is weak or untested
Software is not regularly patched or updated
Alternative troubleshooting methods are available and sufficient
The organization lacks resources for ongoing security monitoring
